title: Conductorize credential pipelines and polish SDK stream facade (py/ts/go) v1.1.0
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: teams building streaming integrations across Python/TypeScript/Go repeatedly implement small, repo-specific credential handoff logic and ad-hoc retry plumbing. This causes duplication and subtle behavioral drift during long-lived streams. This PR introduces a lightweight "Credential Conductor" abstraction plus a streamlined stream facade that standardizes retry, heartbeat and graceful shutdown behavior across SDKs. Key goals: 1) reduce per-language ceremony for credential refresh+failover, 2) normalize default retry predicates for streaming operations (hedged where appropriate), 3) provide a single ergonomic async/iterator surface for consumers, and 4) bump SDK package versions with migration notes.
commits: 3 commits: (1) introduce credential-conductor core interfaces and in-memory orchestrator; (2) wire conductor into py/ts/go stream adapters and add adapter tests; (3) bump package versions and polish changelog/migration notes.

merge_commit: 9e4b7f6 - Conductorize credential pipelines and polish SDK stream facade (squash)
release_notes: Introduces Credential Conductor (py/ts/go) to centralize credential refresh and failover for streaming SDKs. Stabilizes streaming retry/heartbeat behavior and surfaces a unified async/iterator facade. Version bumps: python -> 1.1.0, typescript -> 1.8.3, go -> 1.5.0. Migration guide: docs/sdk/migrations/credential-conductor.md.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on: adapter lifecycle semantics (start/stop/heartbeat), default retry predicates, and public surface changes in each SDK. Heavy testing done in sdk/*/tests and e2e against a private Redwood deployment. The hedged-retry default can be toggled via SDK config if teams need strictly sequential token refresh behavior.
qa_summary: Unit and small-integration tests added across languages. Manual QA: streamed a 20-minute generative session with simulated credential expiry and confirmed conductor performed graceful reauth and resumed without data loss; fallback to secondary credential succeeded under induced primary KMS failure.
migration_tasks:
- Update SDK import paths if you consumed the previous low-level credential helpers (see migration doc).
- If you implemented custom retry logic, evaluate the new default predicates; opt-out flag available.
- Bump pinned SDK versions in downstream services and run quick smoke tests for long-lived streams.
manual_steps_after_merge: 1) Publish new packages: Py wheel -> test.pypi then pypi, TS -> npm, Go -> tag + go proxy. 2) Announce migration guide in #sdk-announce and Slack workspace. 3) Coordinate with SRE for Canary rollout on Dedicated clusters.
authors_note: This PR intentionally keeps the conductor minimal — it is not an orchestrator for multi-tenant state. It is an in-process, per-client helper intended to make common patterns easy and consistent across SDKs. We can extend to a remote coordinator later if customers ask for cross-client session sharing.
